caption:
The Black Death killed roughly a third of Europe's population in just four years — and the continent needed two centuries to get that population back.

Watch Europe's population collapse from ~74 million in 1347 to a low of ~52 million by 1400, then climb, decade after decade, until it finally clears its pre-plague peak around 1550.

📊 See the population of Europe rise, collapse, and recover across three centuries (1300-1600) in this animated trajectory. Explore how the Black Death of 1347-1351 erased a generation of growth in half a decade, why recurring outbreaks kept pushing the total lower into the early 1400s, and how long it really took Europe to reclaim the ground it lost.

Source: Reconstructed series, linearly interpolated between published anchor estimates (1300≈70M, 1347≈74M peak, 1400≈52M, 1500≈67M, 1600≈89M) — synthesis via Encyclopedia.com, consistent with J.C. Russell and O.J. Benedictow; recovery to pre-plague level in the 16th century per Wikipedia/Britannica. Intermediate values are interpolated and indicative only.
